title: The Image of the City (book)
why_it_matters: Kevin Lynch's 1960 study that named paths, edges, districts, nodes and landmarks as the five elements of a legible place.

title: Desire path
why_it_matters: Plain overview of desire lines with examples of planners paving the routes people actually walked.

title: Social force model for pedestrian dynamics
why_it_matters: The model behind most modern crowd simulators: pedestrians as particles pushed by goals and repelled by others.

title: Simulating dynamical features of escape panic
why_it_matters: Shows herding, arching at exits and the faster-is-slower effect that crowd managers plan around.

title: Pedestrian Planning and Design (book)
why_it_matters: John Fruin's original pedestrian level-of-service scale for walkways, stairs and queues.

title: FHWA: Pedestrian level of service tables adapted from Fruin
why_it_matters: Free table of Fruin's LOS A to F thresholds in square metres per pedestrian and flow per metre of width.

title: Crowd density: what 1 to 5 people per square metre look like
why_it_matters: Visual reference from crowd scientist Keith Still for judging density and the safe upper limit of standing crowds.

title: The Hidden Dimension (book)
why_it_matters: Edward T. Hall's proxemics: the intimate, personal, social and public distance zones that queues and vehicles compress.

title: Note on the drawing power of crowds of different size
why_it_matters: Classic street experiment: the more people stare upward, the more passers-by join in. Social proof on a sidewalk.

title: Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion (book)
why_it_matters: Accessible source for social proof and commitment, two levers that shape where guests go and whether they stay in line.

title: Why We Buy: The Science of Shopping (book)
why_it_matters: Paco Underhill's retail observations, including the tendency of shoppers to drift right on entering a space.

title: Making choices impairs subsequent self-control
why_it_matters: The experiments behind decision fatigue: after many choices, people persist less and procrastinate more.

title: Nudge: Improving Decisions About Health, Wealth, and Happiness (book)
why_it_matters: Defines choice architecture and defaults, the toolkit behind reservation systems, park apps and queue entrances.

title: The psychology of sunk cost
why_it_matters: The foundational paper on why people keep investing in something because they already paid for it.

title: Perception of Risk
why_it_matters: Paul Slovic's dread and unknown factors explain why a roller coaster feels riskier than the drive to the park.

title: What Is Rider Switch and How Does It Work? (Walt Disney World)
why_it_matters: Official description of the Party A / Party B procedure that lets families with non-riders take turns.

title: CDC Growth Charts
why_it_matters: Percentile curves for children's height by age, the data behind what a 40-inch or 48-inch rule actually excludes.

title: IAAPA Safety & Security resources
why_it_matters: Industry body's hub for ride safety reports and the idea that safety is a shared responsibility.

title: ASTM F770-22 Standard Practice for Ownership, Operation, Maintenance, and Inspection of Amusement Rides and Devices
why_it_matters: The operations-side standard that frames operator duties, training and patron-facing procedures.

title: Homo Ludens (book)
why_it_matters: Huizinga's idea of the magic circle, the bounded space where play has its own rules, maps neatly onto a themed land.

title: Play: How It Shapes the Brain, Opens the Imagination, and Invigorates the Soul (book)
why_it_matters: Stuart Brown's accessible case for why adults as well as children need free play, with practical play types.

title: What is Ergonomics (HFE)? International Ergonomics Association
why_it_matters: The official definition and the three domains: physical, cognitive and organisational ergonomics.

title: ANSUR II anthropometric dataset (Penn State OPEN Design Lab)
why_it_matters: Free download of the 2012 US Army survey: 6,068 subjects and 93 measurements including hip breadth and sitting height.

title: CAESAR Final Report, Volume I: Summary (US Air Force Research Laboratory, 2002)
why_it_matters: The first large 3D body-scan survey of civilians in the US, the Netherlands and Italy; the civilian counterpart to ANSUR.

title: ASTM F2291 Standard Practice for Design of Amusement Rides and Devices
why_it_matters: The design standard whose Section 5 covers patron restraint, clearance envelope and containment, plus an appendix on riders under 48 inches.

title: Universal Orlando Guide for Rider Safety and Accessibility (PDF)
why_it_matters: Ride-by-ride height limits, health warnings and accessibility notes from a major operator, in one document.

title: NIOSH: About Heat Stress
why_it_matters: Risk factors for heat illness, including sun, humidity, exertion, age and pregnancy, that apply to guests as much as workers.

title: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.95 Occupational noise exposure
why_it_matters: The US rule with the 85 dBA action level and 90 dBA permissible limit that governs ride operators' exposure.

title: NIOSH: About Occupational Hearing Loss
why_it_matters: States the NIOSH recommended exposure limit of 85 dBA over eight hours and why hearing loss is preventable.

title: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design
why_it_matters: The US legal baseline, including sections 234 and 1002 on amusement rides.

title: Guide to the ADA Standards, Chapter 10: Amusement Rides (US Access Board)
why_it_matters: Plain-language guide to wheelchair spaces, transfer seats, transfer devices and load-area rules for new rides.

title: Accessibility Services for Guests with Disabilities (Walt Disney World)
why_it_matters: Operator-side hub for mobility, hearing, visual and cognitive services at a major resort.

title: Disability Access Service (Walt Disney World)
why_it_matters: The official page for DAS, the return-time scheme for guests who cannot wait in a conventional queue.

title: Services for Guests who are Neurodivergent (Walt Disney World)
why_it_matters: Disney's own planning resources for neurodivergent guests, including sensory information about attractions.

title: Certified Autism Center program (IBCCES)
why_it_matters: What CAC certification requires: 80 percent of guest-facing staff trained, onsite review, sensory guides.

title: Sesame Place Makes History With Autism Designation (Philadelphia Magazine, 2018)
why_it_matters: Reports the first theme park to become a Certified Autism Center and the quiet rooms and sensory guide it added.

title: KultureCity Sensory Inclusive certification
why_it_matters: The other common venue certification: staff training, sensory bags, signage and quiet-space modifications.

title: Riding the Black Ship: Japan and Tokyo Disneyland (book)
why_it_matters: Aviad Raz's ethnography of how Tokyo Disneyland was received and reshaped by Japanese guests and staff.

title: "Authentically Disney, distinctly Chinese" and faintly American: The emotional branding of Disneyland in Shanghai
why_it_matters: Academic reading of how Shanghai Disneyland stripped out American references that earlier overseas parks kept.

title: 5 reasons why Shanghai Disneyland is unique (Blooloop)
why_it_matters: Concrete localisation choices: Mickey Avenue instead of Main Street, no Haunted Mansion, a zodiac garden.

title: Hong Kong Disneyland
why_it_matters: Secondary source for the 2005 opening and the feng shui walkway bend near the entrance.

title: Disneyland Paris
why_it_matters: Secondary source for the 1992 opening, the early no-alcohol policy and its 1993 reversal, and adapted menus.

title: Merlin's Magic Wand children's charity
why_it_matters: An operator-linked charity giving park days to children facing illness, disability or hardship; one model of economic inclusion.

title: Walt Disney World theme park tickets
why_it_matters: Shows date-based ticketing in practice, the pricing structure that debates about affordability revolve around.

title: Baby Care Centers (Walt Disney World)
why_it_matters: What a well-run family facility contains: nursing room, changing room, feeding area, kitchenette, supplies.

title: Place illusion and plausibility can lead to realistic behaviour in immersive virtual environments
why_it_matters: Mel Slater's split of presence into place illusion and plausibility illusion, a useful lens for ride design.

title: Enhancing Our Lives with Immersive Virtual Reality
why_it_matters: Open-access review of presence, embodiment and why immersive systems change behaviour.

title: Biographia Literaria (Project Gutenberg)
why_it_matters: The 1817 source of the phrase 'willing suspension of disbelief'.

title: Flow: The Psychology of Optimal Experience (book)
why_it_matters: The original account of flow: clear goals, feedback, and challenge matched to skill.

title: The role of transportation in the persuasiveness of public narratives
why_it_matters: Defines and measures narrative transportation, the state of being lost in a story.

title: The Uncanny Valley (Masahiro Mori, 1970; IEEE Spectrum translation)
why_it_matters: The authorised English translation of the essay that named the uncanny valley.

title: Navigating a social world with robot partners: A quantitative cartography of the Uncanny Valley
why_it_matters: Empirical test with real robot faces showing the valley in likability and in trust.

title: Hamlet on the Holodeck: The Future of Narrative in Cyberspace (book)
why_it_matters: Janet Murray's framing of agency, immersion and transformation in interactive stories.

title: Sally Dark Rides
why_it_matters: A manufacturer's case for interactive gaming in dark rides as the strongest driver of repeat ridership.
